newsitem.title: USA: Dell introduces new pentium servers.
newsitem.headline: Dell introduces new pentium servers.

text.p: AUSTIN, Texas, Sept 9 - Dell Computer Corp introduced a new line of Pentium Pro-based network server computers at prices Dell's chairman and chief executive said will result in an "assault" on the server market.
Chairman and Chief Executive Michael Dell said Dell will use the same direct mail distribution and pricing strategies it used in the desktop market to gain share in the server market.

The first product in the new line, Dell's PowerEdge 2100, is a 200 megahertz, single-processor entry-level server that is as much as 45 percent below the price of many single processor Pentium(R)- based network servers, he said.
Servers are computers that link PCs into small networks and connect other servers to form larger networks.
The 2100 is priced at $3,799 and will be available this month. Dell called it an entry-level to mid-level server, answerable to 85 percent of the server market, he said.
In a few months, Dell plans to introduce a dual-processor PowerEdge 4100, and then the PowerEdge 6100, a multi-processing system for the high end of the market.
"Out belief is that for too long companies built businesses around servers with proprietary technology and attempted to make businesses dependent on them," Dell said.

"We believe we can change all this. We are going to use our direct model (distribution) to deliver servers with open standards and higher-performance, lower-cost components," Dell said, saying the direct mail approach will allow it to pass on to consumers the currently lower cost of chip components. He spoke to reporters in a conference call.
Dell said he expects profit margins in the server industry "to come significantly under pressure because of Dell's initiative," on lower prices.
He said most computer makers subsidize their personal computer and notebook prices by charging high server prices.
"We do not rely on server profit nor do we intend to rely on our server business to subsidize our notebook and desktops," Dell said.
However, he said Dell may see its margins improve if it is able to catch a larger share of the server market.
"We are going to use our servers for market share gain strategy and that will help our desktops and notebooks," he said. The leading server makers are Compaq Computer
Corp, Hewlett-Packard Co and International Business Machines Corp.
